chunks: 4778 - Al-Halabi, Abu Basir, and Sama'ah narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

“And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified a dowry for them, then half of what you have specified must be paid, unless they forgo it or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgoes it.”

He عليه السلام said: “It is the father, or the brother, or the man entrusted with her affairs, and the one whose authority concerning the woman’s property is valid, so he purchases for her and trades; then if he waives it, it is valid.”

key_terms.عَفَا: he waived or remitted the claim
key_terms.عُقْدَةُ ٱلنِّكَاحِ: the bond or contract of marriage
key_terms.فَرَضْتُمْ: you specified or obligated, referring here to the dowry
key_terms.فَرِيضَةً: an assigned obligation, here the designated dowry
key_terms.يَعْفُونَ: they forgo or waive their right
key_terms.يُوصَى إِلَيْهِ: the one entrusted with authority or affairs

ai.seo_question: Who is meant in Qur’an 2:237 by the one in whose hand is the marriage contract?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur’anic phrase about the one in whose hand is the marriage contract in the context of divorce before consummation and after specification of the dowry. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام identifies this as a guardian or authorized person who has recognized authority over the woman’s financial affairs, such that his waiver is legally effective.
